chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: PREFACE I was not poor when I grew up in the 50s, but I know that my family felt cramped.
text_raw:
PREFACE 
I was not poor when I grew up in the 50s, but I know that my 
family felt cramped.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: We had five people in a small house with two bedrooms.
text_raw: We had five people in a small house with two bedrooms.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: My father, a house painter, worked hard and usually steadily, but he probably did not charge his customers enough.
text_raw:
My father, a house painter, worked hard and usually steadily, but he probably 
did not charge his customers enough.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: The family never had a vacation toÂ¬ gether.
text_raw:
The family never had a vacation toÂ¬ 
gether.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I remember my mother using a wooden egg to darn a patch where we had holes in our socks.
text_raw:
I remember my mother using a wooden egg to darn a patch where we 
had holes in our socks.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I have rarely been unemployed.
text_raw: I have rarely been unemployed.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: For most of my high school and college years I worked in the university library or as my fatherâ€™s assistant.
text_raw:
For most of my high school and college 
years I worked in the university library or as my fatherâ€™s assistant.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: I recall that at one point in the early 1960s my dad was paying me $5 an hour; that was the equivalent of more than $30 today.
text_raw:
I recall that at 
one point in the early 1960s my dad was paying me $5 an hour; that was the 
equivalent of more than $30 today.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: My father was too generous as an employer, as he was too generous to his customers.
text_raw:
My father was too generous as an employer, 
as he was too generous to his customers.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: But the high pay for an apprentice house painter seems appropriate to that better time for American workers.
text_raw:
But the high pay for an apprentice 
house painter seems appropriate to that better time for American workers.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Although I suffered only one year of real unemployment in my life, I had more than a decade of worries about keeping the academic position I accepted at California State, Dominguez Hills, in the fall of 1972.
text_raw:
Although I suffered only one year of real unemployment in my life, I had 
more than a decade of worries about keeping the academic position I accepted 
at California State, Dominguez Hills, in the fall of 1972.

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: Californiaâ€™s finances were on a three-decade seesaw, and faculty and staff often worried that they would be laid off.

Californiaâ€™s finances

chapter_title: Frontmatter
text: In the 70s and 80s I participated in meat boycotts, worked with unions, studied the latest inflation and unemployment crises, and learned about Marxism.

In the 70s

In a provocative assessment of American poverty and policy from 1950 to the present, 
Frank Strieker examines an era that has seen serious discussion about the causes of poverty 
and unemployment.

chapter_title: chapter 10 in the present volume and Christopher Howard, The Hidden Welfare State:
text: Analyzing the War on Poverty, theories of the culture of poverty and the underclass, the effects of Reaganomics, and the 1996 welfare reform, Strieker demÂ¬ onstrates that most antipoverty approaches are futile without the presence (or creation) of good jobs.
text_raw:
Analyzing the War on Poverty, theories of the culture of poverty and 
the underclass, the effects of Reaganomics, and the 1996 welfare reform, Strieker demÂ¬ 
onstrates that most antipoverty approaches are futile without the presence (or creation) 
of good jobs.
